'''John Engle Miller III''' (born 1949) is an American [[marine biology|marine biologist]] and retired bishop of the [[Anglican Church in North America]]. He is a former [[Episcopal Church (United States)|Episcopal]] priest who played an active role in the [[Anglican realignment]] in the United States. Consecrated in 2008 to serve as a bishop in the [[Anglican Mission in the Americas]], Miller later served as assisting bishop in the Gulf Atlantic Diocese and provided interim support during episcopal vacancies and leaves of absence in the [[Anglican Diocese of the Great Lakes]] and the [[Anglican Diocese of the Upper Midwest]].

==Early life, education, and marine biology career==
Miller is a native of [[Easton, Pennsylvania]].<ref name="retire">{{cite news |title=The Rt. Rev. John Miller Will Step Down July 12, as Rector of Christ Church Anglican Vero Beach |url=https://www.hometownnewstc.com/news/the-rt-rev-john-miller-will-step-down-july-12-as-rector-of-christ-church/article_444aab38-9846-11e9-9d36-37badbd38add.html |access-date=28 November 2022 |work=Hometown News |date=June 27, 2019}}</ref> He received his B.A. in [[zoology]] from the [[University of South Florida]], where he also did graduate studies in marine biology in 1965.<ref name="amia-leadership">{{cite web |title=Our Structure and Leadership |url=http://www.theamia.org///experience/structure-leadership |website=Anglican Mission in the Americas |access-date=27 November 2022 |date=2008 |archive-date=21 November 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081121163309/http://www.theamia.org///experience/structure-leadership |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref> Miller worked as a marine biologist at the [[Smithsonian Institution]] in Washington and the [[Harbor Branch Oceanographic Institute]] in [[Fort Pierce, Florida]], for eighteen years. His research was conducted from Bermuda to Antarctica and throughout the Caribbean Sea.<ref name="retire" /> He is married to Joyce and they have three adult children.<ref name="amia-leadership" />

In 1990, Miller enrolled in [[Trinity School for Ministry]]. While there, he and his wife Joyce were spiritually influenced by the discipleship ministry of [[Thad Barnum|Thad and Erilynne Barnum]] in Aliquippa. Miller graduated in 1993 with an M.Div. and was ordained in the [[Episcopal Diocese of Central Florida]].<ref name="amia-leadership" /> 

==Ordained ministry==

Miller served as assistant rector and school chaplain at [[Holy Trinity Episcopal Church (Melbourne, Florida)|Holy Trinity Episcopal Church]] in [[Melbourne, Florida]], in 1994, and as priest in charge from 1994 to 1996. From 1996 to 2004, he was rector of St. John's Episcopal Church in Melbourne.<ref name="amia-leadership" /> In 2004, he left the Episcopal Church and joined the Anglican Mission in the Americas, planting Prince of Peace Anglican Church in Melbourne.<ref name="st-john">{{cite news |title=CENTRAL FLORIDA: St. John's Departure from the Episcopal Church |url=https://virtueonline.org/central-florida-st-johns-departure-episcopal-church |access-date=28 November 2022 |work=Virtue Online |date=2004}}</ref> By 2008, Prince of Peace Anglican had grown to 400 members.<ref name="amia-leadership" />

In 2007, the Rwandan bishops elected Miller to serve as a missionary bishop in the AMIA. He was consecrated in January 2008 by [[Emmanuel Kolini]] alongside [[Terrell Glenn (bishop)|Terrell Glenn]] and Philip Jones.<ref name="amia-bishop">{{cite web |title=The Anglican Mission Celebrates Appointment of New Missionary Bishops |url=http://www.theamia.org/newsitem/123 |website=Anglican Mission in the Americas |access-date=27 November 2022 |date=2007 |archive-date=10 December 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071210032556/http://www.theamia.org/newsitem/123 |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref> Miller oversaw a network of more than 30 AMIA congregations in Florida, Georgia, and Alabama<ref name="gad-profile">{{cite web |title=Meet the Team |url=https://www.gulfatlanticdiocese.org/meet-the-team |website=Gulf Atlantic Diocese |access-date=28 November 2022}}</ref> while remaining rector of Prince of Peace, as was customary for AMIA bishops.<ref name="amia-bishop" />

In 2010, AMIA—which had been a founding member of the ACNA the year before—left full membership, changing its status in ACNA to "ministry partner."<ref name="aac-amia-breakdown">{{cite news |last1=Lundy |first1=Robert H. |title=Anglican Mission in the Americas: The Aftermath |url=http://www.americananglican.org/anglican-mission-in-the-americas-the-aftermath-2 |access-date=21 November 2022 |work=Encompass |issue=First Quarter 2012 |publisher=American Anglican Council |archive-date=30 May 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130530221242/http://www.americananglican.org/anglican-mission-in-the-americas-the-aftermath-2 |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref> By the next year, the relationship between AMIA chairman Murphy and the Anglican Church of Rwanda's house of bishops, led by Kolini's successor [[Onesphore Rwaje]], had broken down over questions of financial transparency and collegiality.<ref name="episcopal-4">{{cite book |author1=Terrell L. Glenn |editor1-last=Arten |editor1-first=Isaac |editor2-last=Glass |editor2-first=William |title=A House Divided? Ways Forward for North American Anglicans |date=2015 |publisher=Wipf and Stock |page=64 |chapter=A Unity Greater Than Doctrine}}</ref> Except for Glenn and Barnum, the AMIA bishops removed AMIA from Rwandan jurisdiction and restructured it as a "missionary society."<ref name="amia-collapse">{{cite news |last1=Virtue |first1=David |title=An Unholy Mess: Clash of Wills, Power Struggles, & Theological Direction Mark AMIA-ACNA Struggle |url=https://theaquilareport.com/an-unholy-mess-clash-of-wills-power-struggles-theological-direction-mark-amia-acna-struggle/ |access-date=21 November 2022 |work=Virtue Online |date=October 9, 2012}}</ref> In the fallout from AMIA's break with ACNA and Rwanda, some AMIA bishops—including Miller—transitioned directly into the ACNA.<ref name="amia-collapse" /> 

Miller accepted a call in 2012 as rector of Christ Church in [[Vero Beach, Florida|Vero Beach]], a four-year-old congregation in the recently formed Gulf Atlantic Diocese, where Miller was appointed assisting bishop.<ref name="retire" /><ref name="gad-profile" /> Miller was restored to membership in the ACNA College of Bishops in 2013.<ref name="restore-acna-cob">{{cite web |title=A COMMUNIQUE FROM THE COLLEGE OF BISHOPS OF THE ANGLICAN CHURCH IN NORTH AMERICA |url=https://anglicanchurch.net/a-communique-from-the-college-of-bishops-of-the-anglican-church-in-north-america/ |website=Anglican Church in North America |access-date=28 November 2022 |date=June 22, 2013}}</ref> In 2017, Miller presided over the dedication of a new 27,000-square-foot facility for Christ Church,<ref name="ccvb-construction">{{cite news |last1=Trudell |first1=Tracy |title=Christ Church complex nears completion |url=https://www.tcpalm.com/story/specialty-publications/your-news/st-lucie-county/reader-submitted/2017/05/22/christ-church-complex-nears-completion/337408001/ |access-date=28 November 2022 |work=TCPalm |date=May 22, 2017}}</ref> and in 2019, he retired as rector of Christ Church.<ref name="retire" /> 

==Later life==
In retirement, Miller took on interim roles across the ACNA. From 2019 to 2020, he was interim bishop of the Diocese of the Great Lakes during the episcopal vacancy between [[Ronald Jackson (bishop)|Ronald Jackson]] and [[Mark Engel (bishop)|Mark Engel]].<ref name="adgl">{{cite news |title=Interim bishop of the Diocese of the Great Lakes steps down |url=https://anglican.ink/2020/03/17/interim-bishop-of-the-diocese-of-the-great-lakes-steps-down/ |access-date=28 November 2022 |work=Anglican Ink |date=March 17, 2020}}</ref> From 2021 to 2022, after allegations of mishandling of abuse reports, Miller was acting bishop in the Diocese of the Upper Midwest, appointed by ACNA Primate [[Foley Beach]] and with delegated authority from the UMD's Bishop's Council during [[Stewart Ruch]]'s leave of absence.<ref name="umd">{{cite news |title=Miller and Atkinson appointed acting bishops of the Upper Midwest |url=https://anglican.ink/2021/07/28/miller-and-atkinson-appointed-acting-bishops-of-the-upper-midwest/ |access-date=28 November 2022 |work=Anglican Ink |date=July 28, 2021}}</ref>

Miller also serves as a "[[pastoral care|soul care]]" counselor for clergy in partnership with Thad Barnum.<ref name="gad-profile" />
